words.definition: A child of your uncle or aunt.
words.example: My cousin and I grew up in the same town and played together every weekend.
words.mnemonic: Your aunt’s son or daughter is your cousin.

words.definition: Happy to give more money, time, or help than is usual or expected.
words.example: My grandmother is very generous and always cooks extra food for the neighbors.
words.mnemonic: Generous people "generate" smiles by sharing what they have.

words.definition: Someone or something that you can trust to work well or do what they promise.
words.example: She is my most reliable friend—whenever I need help, she is always there on time.
words.mnemonic: Rely + able: someone you are able to rely on.

words.definition: The way a child is cared for and taught how to behave by their parents while growing up.
words.example: Despite having a strict upbringing, he remained very close to his parents.
words.mnemonic: How your parents "bring you up" from a baby to an adult.

words.definition: Able to understand and share the feelings of another person as if they were your own.
words.example: A good listener is empathetic and tries to see the problem from your point of view.
words.mnemonic: Empathy = feeling "in" someone else’s heart.

words.definition: A person that you work with at your job.
words.example: I usually have lunch with my colleagues at a small cafe near our office.
words.mnemonic: Co (together) + league: people in the same work league as you.

words.definition: A time or day by which something must be finished.
words.example: We need to finish the design report before Friday’s deadline.
words.mnemonic: The final line on the calendar when the project must be done.

words.definition: To give someone a higher or more important position at work.
words.example: After two years of hard work, the company decided to promote her to team manager.
words.mnemonic: Pro (forward) + move: moving forward and up in your career.

words.definition: To discuss something formally in order to reach an agreement on price, salary, or terms.
words.example: Don’t be afraid to negotiate your starting salary when you receive a new job offer.
words.mnemonic: Talking things through until both sides say "Okay, deal!"

words.definition: Able to recover quickly and stay strong after difficult problems or changes.
words.example: Small businesses had to be very resilient when customer habits changed overnight.
words.mnemonic: Like a rubber ball that bounces right back after hitting the floor.

words.definition: The bags and suitcases that you take with you when you travel.
words.example: We left our heavy luggage at the hotel reception and walked to the beach.
words.mnemonic: From "lug" (to carry something heavy)—the bags you lug around on a trip.

words.definition: A person who is traveling in a car, bus, train, or plane, but is not driving or flying it.
words.example: All passengers must show their boarding pass before getting on the plane.
words.mnemonic: Someone "passing" through on a journey.

words.definition: The place where someone is going or where something is being sent.
words.example: After a six-hour train ride, we finally arrived at our holiday destination.
words.mnemonic: Destiny + nation: the place you are destined to arrive at.

words.definition: A detailed plan or list of places you will visit on a trip.
words.example: Our tour guide sent us the daily itinerary, including museum visits and boat trips.
words.mnemonic: Your step-by-step "tiny diary" of where you’ll go each day on vacation.

words.definition: Beautiful and charming to look at, like a painted picture (especially of an old town or village).
words.example: We stayed in a picturesque fishing village surrounded by green hills and clear water.
words.mnemonic: Picture + esque: so pretty it looks just like a postcard picture!

words.definition: Someone who lives very near you, especially in the next house or apartment.
words.example: Our next-door neighbor watered our plants while we were away for the weekend.
words.mnemonic: The person living "near-by" your door.

words.definition: Easy to use, helpful, or near a place so it saves you time and effort.
words.example: Living near the subway station is very convenient for getting to work every morning.
words.mnemonic: Think of a "convenience store" right on the corner—quick and easy!

words.definition: A regular job that you have to do at home, such as washing dishes or cleaning the floor.
words.example: On Saturday mornings, we share the household chores so the apartment stays tidy.
words.mnemonic: Chores can feel like a "bore", but they keep the house clean!

words.definition: Large and having plenty of room to move around in.
words.example: The new apartment has a spacious living room with big windows and lots of sunlight.
words.mnemonic: Full of "space" = spacious.

words.definition: Very careful and paying great attention to every small detail.
words.example: He is meticulous about organizing his desk so he can find any document in seconds.
words.mnemonic: Checking every single "tick" of a clock with a magnifying glass.

words.definition: Having a very pleasant taste or smell.
words.example: The fresh warm bread from the bakery smelled and tasted delicious.
words.mnemonic: Delight + dish = a delicious dish!

words.definition: One of the foods or items that you put together to make a particular dish.
words.example: Fresh tomatoes, basil, and olive oil are the main ingredients in this pasta sauce.
words.mnemonic: The things that go "in" the pot when you cook.

words.definition: Food that looks or smells so good that it makes you want to eat it immediately.
words.example: The colorful fruit salad looked so appetizing on a hot summer afternoon.
words.mnemonic: Gives you a big "appetite" as soon as you see or smell it!

words.definition: Extremely tired, having no energy left at all.
words.example: After walking twenty kilometers around the city, we were completely exhausted.
words.mnemonic: Like a car that has used up all its fuel through the exhaust pipe.

words.definition: Worried and nervous about something that may happen in the future.
words.example: It is normal to feel a little anxious the night before an important speaking exam.
words.mnemonic: Taking a deep breath helps calm an anxious mind.

words.definition: Having two opposite feelings at the same time, so you are not sure what you want.
words.example: She felt ambivalent about moving abroad—excited for the adventure, but sad to leave her friends.
words.mnemonic: Ambi means "both"—pulled in both directions at once.

words.definition: To get better, or to make something better.
words.example: Reading short stories in English every evening helped me improve my vocabulary quickly.
words.mnemonic: Practice every day to prove you can improve!

words.definition: To give all your attention to what you are doing and not think about other things.
words.example: I put my phone in another room so I can concentrate on my homework.
words.mnemonic: Bring all your thoughts into the "center" of one task.

words.definition: To make a problem or bad effect less harmful or less serious.
words.example: Planting more trees in cities helps mitigate the effects of summer heat.
words.mnemonic: Soft mittens make a freezing winter day much less harsh.

words.definition: Seen or found everywhere at the same time; very common.
words.example: Coffee shops and smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern city life.
words.mnemonic: Think of Wi-Fi signals floating everywhere around you.
